I've beaten the game with all classes, so I clearly enjoyed what was here. I am a little disappointed, though, coming from the excellent demo. [strike]At the end of each run in the demo, you could win the game and then compete against your previous 'best' build to see what would come out on top. That led me to actually put more hours into the demo than the game I paid money for. Why isn't that function here?[/strike] EDIT: This has been addressed and fixed! There's also an issue with balance that becomes much more evident in the later stages. Early on, you can experiment with any type of build (shield, poison, magic) and create interesting solutions. By the end game, though, the only way to consistently win is to invest in shield units. One of the late game bosses completely shuts down magic for some reason, even though magic is by far the weakest of the three main build types. And there are plenty of enemies towards the end that will just one shot units unless you've invested in shields for everyone -- no one's health permanently increases enough to outpace the enemy's damage scaling. There aren't enough incentives to try and waste build space with magic/poison when it's a) random that you'll even get the most vital pieces to support it and b) too weak to overcome the enemy's late game defenses. The demon and unit that gets a shield every time it takes magic damage need to be completely reworked, because as-is they basically just say "Ha! You didn't make everyone have shields? GG." So, after all of that, why am I still recommending it? Because I still feel like it has a lot of promise. I was super excited for the release and while it didn't quite live up to my expectations, I understand it's early access and more is to come. If balance continues to be an issue even after patches, and there isn't more end game content for people that already unlocked all six classes, then I'll have to change my recommendation. But for now, I'm still tentatively positive about it.

It's good, I like it. The mechanics are interesting and everything goes together quite well. My gripes are that; 1: It's way too easy, 3 ish hours took me to a win with every hero, and it was first try every time apart from once with the basic hero. Once you know how the game works it's very easy to draft an incredibly powerful team. 2: The first and last "stages" are totally irrelevant, first is an auto win with the stuff you start with, and the last one is just the very easy boss. The rest is all likely just early access complaints so take these without too much notice; The enemy variety is very slim, end boss is always the same and there must be 2 enemy "heroes" for each area. End boss is 20/500 with 6 lives, he has to face your 8 souped up minions with no other tricks. At one point I had a unit with 12000 damage, come on boss get your socks on!| Anyway all of those complaints, I enjoyed the game a lot, it can only get better.

It is a very good auto battler, where you select the cards and spells randomly from a choice of 3 to 5. It needs more content for the current price, but would be very fair at $9.99 in its present form and might even sell better at that price. It is still early access and so I hope to see more in the next few months. I recommend trying the demo like I did, and you will know if you like it within an hour. To the developers: There are some great components here, but more is needed. I recommend a mode where you start with the spell that lets you select the attacker/blocker to appease people who like deciding where the attacker attacks instead of leaving to the randomness of an auto battler. (This spell already exists, so it would be an easy mode to add from a programming standpoint.) More cards, more heroes and more variant enemies are needed, but I have enjoyed the game a ton so far.

1.0 release is an absolute mess. The UI in a lot of the menus is atrocious and clips on top of other parts of the menu (which was excusable in Early Access but definitely isn't for 1.0), no option to have multiple profiles and you can't reset the progress to experience the 1.0 game without prior early access progress either. It doesn't feel like they reached 1.0, it feels like they just decided to call it a day and slap it on top of what was there. Some of the arts seemed incomplete, fine for early access, not for 1.0 No easy way to access the speed up feature from combat instead of going to the menu and selecting from a drop down, fine for early access, not so much for 1.0 Buggy settings menu (mine has text saying "restart game for display changes to take effect" even after restarting and the display changes have already taken effect, yet the text is still there, bugged under the concede run button). Again, fine for early access, not OK for 1.0 No proper way to tell what kind of abilities some enemies have at a glance (ie, there's an icon for shield and ranged effects but there isn't one for "cleave" or round start, or most effects really, so you just have to hover over every enemy and memorize all of them), once more, fine for an early access title, not really standard quality for a 1.0 release. When you click a game mode (for example, Coliseum), you're presented with the selection of different characters. From there, there is no "back" button; you can't go back to the mode selection menu (like you would in literally any other game), the only way to go back is to go to the settings menu and "concede run". Really. The game modes are poorly edited PNGs with a bunch of white stray pixels on the edges of the image in low resolution (they didn't bother cutting around them in Photoshop or anything before dragging and dropping it onto the engine).1.0 game. Under all of this there is a good indie game with fun synergies, mind you, it's just been apparently abandoned and labeled 1.0 for all I could tell.

Tempting as it may be to go for the meme of using the game's vernacular of a smugly sarcastic "Good Effort" that it loves to throw at you when you fail to beat what I assume to be another player's usually broken boardstate in a futile attempt to improve your minions, I'm well aware that being PURELY snippy doesn't help to improve games - which I would very much like to see in this case, because the game does GENUINELY have an interesting concept, a good art style, and some really neat ideas. The problem, however, is the balance, because while the game does feature a lot of options, they are most assuredly not made equal. The game features a variety of six different necromancers, each focusing on their own gameplay style, all thematically belonging to one of the six factions of minions you get access to - not that they're necessarily GOOD with their faction of minion, which I already have some thoughts about, but it goes beyond that, because the inherent passives of the necromancers swing wildly between "Fun, effective and flavorful" all the way to "mindnumbingly tedious", taking a brief stop in the center of mediocrity in the process. "You get one Skull (the game's currency) when you merge minions"? Dull. Starting minion is a "stat stick" with no abilities, whose only claim to being a stat stick is having 3/2 instead of 2/2. This thing will not scale, it will never be useful in any capacity. Minions attacking with their HP instead of their attack? Kind of neat, shakes up the gameplay, feels unique. Good. Also starts with a minion with a unique ability that scales decently well into the late game - 0/2 that deals its' HP's worth of magic damage at the start of the fight. Fused versions can improve this ability to get up to 4 of these magic attacks, and HP scaling is easy enough. Fun. Decent. Flavorful. Good. "Merge any two minions together to create a patchwork abomination"? Cool in concept, thematically fitting for zombies. Decent starting minion too. It works okay, usually, if RNG plays nice and you get to make something broken. And therein lies the problem. The game is seemingly so balanced around the fact that you can break it that any run where you DON'T break the game just feels mindnumbingly dull bordering on unfair at times, because the main difficulty increases are "Enemy has more Attack and Health now". Every character with a gimmick is balanced around breaking the game using said gimmick, and the ones that aren't - i.e. the ones that get better Skull economy or the likes - are pretty much just getting more rerolls to get the minions that break the game more easily. The Necroforager starts with a minion that, when recycled, gives you an extra skull in addition to the one you always get for recycling. Her passive is that summoning a minion triggers its recycling abilities. So she can recycle her starting minion to get 3 skulls - enough for a reroll, and a purchase of another of her starting minions. Which she can then recycle, to reroll - or, if it's there, buy another starting minion to acquire 4 skulls. So the ideal play with her is to sit around and recycling, rerolling, recycling, rerolling, recycling and rerolling until she starts with a full board of upgraded minions, all at the low, low cost of up to 10 minutes of your lifespan and braincells. You [i]CAN[/i] play the game normally as her - you just won't feel like she has anything special going on until halfway into the run, and the game will likely kick your teeth in for not abusing her unique flavor, because while Level 1 is usually painfully dull and you have to actively try to lose lives, Level 2 is where the game starts throwing enemies at you that can have pretty harsh gimmicks - and by Level 3 you're getting things like "At the start of each combat, target a random minion - it punches a minion next to it", which can result in the worst case in two dead minions, while the enemy has a board stacked with 10/30 critters. Does it still sound the 3/2 skeleton man is gonna pull his weight in any capacity, compared to, say, the "nuke random enemy 4 time with your HP which, with the necromancer's ability, is also your attack stat"? It's just a starting minion, of course, but it's a throughline with all the minions. Since every necromancer has access to every faction and no faction's minions as a whole lend themselves entirely well to any one necromancer's gimmick - sometimes even working directly against it - there's no point to going for anything actually thematic; there's no strategic choices to consider because you're not locked out of any faction; monogamy is enforced by certain relics, minions and their "buff all [i]related[/i] minions"-abilities, rather than necromancers and their being literally representatives of a faction; it's RNG whether you get to play mushrooms or not. The skeleton guy can summon as many pumpkins as the pumpkin guy, and the fungus woman can have a full board of spirits, horrors and zombies with no mushrooms in sight. With no restrictions that might help hone in on a faction, and no real bonuses to any one necromancer's faction, you just snap up the minions you know have the capacity to be broken with your necromancer's passive ability, and the rest of these nicely drawn, cute or cool or funny little creatures with nicely written lore fall by the wayside after you try them once to unlock their bestiary entry, notice they just don't work, and in an act as callous and sad as throwing out an old teddy because you no longer have space for it in your serious adult life, you ignore them going forward. Sorry, Void Champion; your "deal magic damage to ALL combatants including your own"-ability just doesn't gel well with the void-necromancers "all minions deal damage with their current HP"-passive. No room on the bus for you. And minions really are the main way to work with your run. Relics VERY rarely change up enough to be worth considering a "Wow, that's great", and the other options in-between levels... don't do much. +1 Magic damage? Alright, neat. +1/+1 to any given minion, double if you beat what I assume is some random player's board? At least that one scales to +2/+2, +3/+3 etc. per floor. "All minions in shops get +1/+0 or +0/+1"? Insultingly pointless, and that RNG can just decree that's one of the options you have to take is an affront to the laws of both man, nature and God. Doesn't even scale with the Level you're on. The overuse of sarcasm to get displeasure with points across effectively over the internet may lead you to believe that I hate this game. I don't. It's got a neat concept. Necromancers are objectively cool. And I SERIOUSLY hope the issues can be ironed out, because it's mostly some numbers tweaks, and maybe some restrictions or bonuses here or there to get some flavor across. How about choices between starting relics that grant varying buffs to playstyles? Horrors tend to either have a lot of HP, or deal magic damage, but only one of those is relevant to the Horror-necromancer; why not add an option that benefits from self-destructive shenanigans like the Void Champions "blow everything up"? Fungi love poison - why not give the Forager an option to lean into it more rather than the "summon and recycle"-shenanigans? Maybe an option to "banish" a faction from a given run, to make it more likely you get your faction going, or restrict what factions any given necromancer has access to? There are easy ways to make this game have more depth, more options, more [i]flavor[/i] rather than letting most of it fizzle out in mediocrity because it doesn't excel or simply can't break things hard enough. And I really hope it's looked into, because I swear this on my honor, I will sing this game's praises as eagerly as I criticised it the very second something changes. For now, though, I don't recommend it. [i]For now[/i].

I'd hold off on this one for now. I', nearing the 10 hour mark and feel like I've exhausted my interest in the game, even though I love auto battlers and the entire premise of this game. There's just not enough unlocks or enemy diversity yet to keep you interested for long. That being said, it's a great foundation for an auto-battler and I enjoy the art and theme, so this review could change with time and new content. The fact that this ISN'T in early access though leaves me nervous about that possibility, though. At the very least, wait for a good sale. EDITed over a year later: They did not, in fact, update anything about this game after the lone post launch patch. Avoid it, not worth the money.
